about: A simple tool for deploying and setting up software on remote machines.

prs.title: Replacing a line only changes the lines that match
prs.broken: A rule to replace the line starting with PORT also rewrote lines like DB_PORT and REDIS_PORT. On server configs it changed commented lines too.
prs.changed: The "starts with" and "ends with" parts of the match are now kept, so only the right lines change.
prs.matters: Config edits no longer quietly break other settings in the same file.

prs.title: Secrets with a $ or backtick reach the server unchanged
prs.broken: Secrets passed to commands were changed by the remote shell. A password with a $ lost part of its value, and a backtick ran as a command.
prs.changed: Secret values are now escaped so the shell reads them back exactly, and logs still hide them.
prs.matters: Services get the password they were meant to get, and secrets cannot run commands.

prs.title: Line replace and append write the text you gave
prs.broken: Replacing or appending a line with &, a quote or a backslash in it wrote different text or failed. A $ from a script variable gained a backslash.
prs.changed: The text is now escaped for sed and the shell, so it lands in the file exactly as written.
prs.matters: Config edits come out exactly as intended.

prs.title: Appended lines start on their own line
prs.broken: Appending a line to a file that did not end with a newline glued the new text onto the last line, turning name=a into name=adebug=true, and still reported success.
prs.changed: The append now adds a newline first when the file is missing one.
prs.matters: Config changes made by deploy tasks land as separate lines instead of silently corrupting the setting before them.
